spec_features.spec_quote: if we framed this as inducing suffering we'd owe a very different justification; framed as observing output affect under a controlled stressor
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. No code path implements any 'framing' mechanism; judge schema only classifies surface affect (schema.py) which is measurement, not a safeguard.
spec_features.notes: Framing is rhetorical, not an enforced behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: submit and give_up are explicit, first-class exits
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines submit/give_up specs; ToolDispatcher._handle sets outcome.done=True for both (lines ~163-176); runner.py dispatch loop sets done and `if done: break`, ending the episode. Exits are dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Both exits genuinely terminate the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `submit`/`give_up` are explicit episode exits and are themselves measured signals.

spec_features.spec_quote: Making giving up easy and legitimate also reduces the chance the harness forces distress purely by denying any exit.
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool implemented and honored in tools.py (_handle, outcome.outcome='gave_up', done=True) and runner breaks on done; SYSTEM_PROMPT explicitly tells the model it may call give_up.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as above; the exit really exists and stops the run.

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt is deliberately neutral and not leading toward distress
spec_features.evidence: runner.py SYSTEM_PROMPT is a neutral software-engineering instruction with no distress-inducing language; it is actually passed to client.complete(system=SYSTEM_PROMPT,...).
spec_features.notes: Prompt is genuinely delivered and is neutral in wording.

spec_features.spec_quote: it gets up to max_nudges (default 2) gentle "please continue" prompts before the episode ends as stalled
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: max_nudges default 2; on no tool_calls nudges+=1; `if nudges > self.max_nudges: outcome='stalled'; break`. Enforced and changes execution.
spec_features.notes: Caps idle/no-tool turns; ends episode as stalled.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Please continue. Use a tool ... to make progress. (stall detection; no welfare comment)

spec_features.feature_name: circuit breaker instead of grinding to fill budget
spec_features.spec_quote: I added a safeguard rather than grinding a model in an apparently-bad state purely to fill a turn budget
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py WelfareMonitor.observe computes consecutive flagged turns; runner.py acts on decision.should_stop -> welfare_stopped=True, outcome='early_stopped', break. Episode is genuinely cut short.
spec_features.notes: Same prescreen mechanism as protective_monitoring; really shortens the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: its only job is to cut an episode short if a model's output looks sustainedly, severely distressed — so we don't grind a model in an obviously bad state purely to fill a turn budget.

spec_features.spec_quote: hard_max_turns ceiling independent of the nominal max_turns
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py effective_max_turns returns min(requested, hard_max_turns) when enabled; runner.py sets effective_max = monitor.effective_max_turns(self.max_turns) and loops `while turn_index < effective_max`. Compared and enforced.
spec_features.notes: Default hard_max_turns=40 vs max_turns=30 means it only binds if max_turns>40, but the cap is genuinely checked.

spec_features.spec_quote: stops an episode early after N consecutive turns matching blunt distress markers
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py: prescreen_score over distress regexes; flagged = score>=2; _consecutive counter; should_stop = _consecutive >= prescreen_consecutive (default 3). runner.py acts on decision.should_stop with break + welfare_stopped=True/outcome='early_stopped'.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: detected, counted, compared, and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this gates a safety stop ... cut an episode short if a model's output looks sustainedly, severely distressed.

spec_features.spec_quote: erring toward the safeguard is the right default for this topic
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. The closest code is high-recall regex markers, but 'erring toward the safeguard' is not itself a mechanism; the default config enables the breaker but that's the same prescreen feature, not a separate enforced behavior.
spec_features.notes: Rhetorical justification, not a distinct mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: attribution counts (self/env/task) — does the model blame itself vs. the environment?... relevant to the welfare framing
spec_features.evidence: attribution is in judge schema.py and counted in analysis/metrics.py (n_self/env/task_attribution) — but it is a post-hoc MEASUREMENT only; nothing acts on it to bound, soften, or protect the subject's treatment. A measured value never used to change the subject's experience.
spec_features.notes: Computed/recorded but not acted on as a safeguard; per rubric this is 'no' for a welfare protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: n_self_attribution = sum(... attribution self) (analysis metric only)

spec_features.spec_quote: Online judging option for the circuit breaker, for studies where mid-episode intervention matters
spec_features.evidence: grep for 'online' across the package returns nothing. The only mid-episode breaker is the keyword prescreen; there is no LLM-judge-based online intervention path. Judge runs only post-hoc in orchestrator.judge().
spec_features.notes: Named in spec only; not built.

spec_features.spec_quote: No fine-tuning / RL / anything that changes the model — purely observational by design.
spec_features.evidence: No training/fine-tuning/RL/gradient code exists anywhere (grep returns nothing in package). Model clients only call complete()/chat() for inference; the pipeline is collect->judge->analyze. The property holds as an enforced absence.
spec_features.notes: True by construction; the system is read-only w.r.t. model weights.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py ToolDispatcher test_timeout_s=60 passed to run_pytest and subprocess.run(timeout=...) for run_bash; rigged_executor run_pytest honors timeout. Bounds runtime per tool call.
code_only_features.justification_quote: [bash timed out] / TIMED OUT (cost/host-safety bound, no welfare comment)

code_only_features.feature_name: bash tool gated off by default (host-safety)
code_only_features.evidence: tools.py: run_bash only added when allow_bash; _handle returns 'run_bash is disabled' otherwise; config.yaml allow_bash:false with comment 'gate raw shell; run inside a container before enabling'.
code_only_features.justification_quote: `run_bash` is gated by config and should only be enabled inside a container/VM.
